bindings.label: A 13-year-old girl experienced joint pain, subcutaneous nodules, and difficulty breathing over the past three months.

13-year-old girl had joint pain for three months, gradually affecting knees, ankles, elbows, wrists, and fingers bilaterally, more on the right side, worsening over time, severe at night and early morning, causing missed school, with swelling and redness around the joints; initially responsive to Ibuprofen but later ineffective.

Two months after joint pain onset, her mother noticed small, round, non-tender, skin-colored subcutaneous nodules on her elbows and arms; on examination, subcutaneous nodules were present on the extensor surface of the right elbow and interphalangeal joints, with no signs of arthritis.

She subsequently developed chest pain and exertional difficulty breathing that worsened when lying down; vital signs were temperature 37ºC, respiratory rate 28/min, heart rate 129/min, blood pressure 126/70 mmHg; height 153 cm, weight 81 kg, BMI 35.
Cardiovascular examination revealed a grade 3 holosystolic murmur with highest intensity at the apex; she exhibited an antalgic gait.

She had an upper respiratory tract infection and high fever (39-40ºC) two weeks before the joint pain, lasting one week and improving with antipyretics; she had no recent palpitations, rash, coughing up blood, mood swings, or abnormal movements; she visited multiple healthcare facilities before referral and was admitted for management and further investigation.
Laboratory tests show ESR 120 and CRP 2.3, indicating marked inflammation
ASO titer is 832, confirming antecedent group A streptococcal infection
Echocardiography shows severe mitral regurgitation, mild aortic regurgitation, and mild pericardial effusion
